source: Belfield, S. and Brown, C. (2010). Guidebook on Upland Crops in Cambodia: Corn (សៀវភៅណែនាំ ស្តីពីដំណាំតំបន់ខ្ពង់រាបនៅក្នុងប្រទេសកម្ពុជា៖ ដំណាំពោត). ACIAR Monograph 143, published by the Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research (ACIAR) in partnership with NSW Department of Primary Industries, the Cambodian Agricultural Research and Development Institute (CARDI), Murdoch University, University of Canberra, and MAFF, under ACIAR Project ASEM/2000/109. Uploaded PDF, 52 pages, image-only (Limon-font-era scan, read via page rasterization).
text:
Reference glossary of scientific and English common names for insect pests of corn mentioned across MAFF/ACIAR materials for Cambodia:

- Achaea janata -- Castor oil looper
- Acherontia styx -- Eastern death's head hawk moth
- Cletus bipunctatus -- Spined legume bug
- Conogethes punctiferalis -- Yellow peach moth / castor borer
- Helicoverpa armigera -- Heliothis, corn earworm
- Hypomeces squamosus -- Gold dust weevil
- Microtermes sp., Hypotermes sp., Globitermes sp., Macrotermes gilvus -- Root-cutting termite
- Nezara viridula -- Green vegetable bug
- Omoides abstitalis -- Legume webspinner
- Ostrinia furnacalis, Sesamia inferens -- Asian maize borer
- Riptortus sp. -- Brown bean bug
- Rhopalosiphum maidis -- Green peach aphid
- Myzus persicae -- Maize aphid
- Spodoptera litura -- Cluster caterpillar
- Spoladea recurvalis -- Beet webworm

Note: the original source table also gives a Khmer common name for each entry (and, for several species, two alternate Khmer names reflecting regional naming variation). Those Khmer labels are omitted here rather than risk an inaccurate transcription, since short table-label Khmer text is easy to mis-read at the source scan's resolution and this glossary's value depends on getting each name exactly right; a future session with clearer source access should add the verified Khmer names.
